---
title: "How to use this course"
---

This is the machine learning course that first-year students of [Applied Data Science & AI](https://ai.buas.nl/) at Breda University of Applied Sciences take, adapted for independent learning. It is free, with no registration, no deadlines and no certificate. You decide how far you go.

The course has three parts (see the [overview](index.qmd#course-structure)):

- **Self-study**: notebooks and reading guides that teach the concepts;
- **DataLab**: a client project in three iterations, where you apply them to real molecules;
- **Assessment**: two Kaggle competitions (stability and energy levels) that score your predictions on molecules you haven't seen.

## Choose your path

### Just reading

Read the pages and notebooks here on the website. Nothing to install. The notebooks show the code and, in the first theme, its output. Start with [What is Machine Learning?](self-study/00_what_is_machine_learning.qmd), which you can try out in your browser. You will understand the ideas, but you only really learn machine learning by writing the code yourself.

### A quick look in Google Colab

Every notebook page has an **Open in Colab** button that runs the notebook in your browser. Good for trying a few notebooks. For the whole course, Colab is not practical: it forgets the files you create, and the DataLab notebooks build on each other's files.

### The full course (recommended)

[Set up your computer](setup.qmd) once (about 15 minutes), then follow the [course route](#the-course-route) below: Self-study and DataLab in turn, every exercise in the notebooks, and at the end your own models on the Kaggle leaderboards.

### You already know machine learning

Go to the project. Read the [Business Understanding](datalab/iteration-1/01_business_understanding.qmd) and [Data Understanding](datalab/iteration-1/02_data_understanding.qmd) pages for the problem and the data, skim the Iteration 2 notebooks on [reading the HOPV file](datalab/iteration-2/02_understanding_homolumo_data.ipynb) and [computing molecular descriptors](datalab/iteration-2/03_data_preparation.ipynb), then start [Iteration 3+](datalab/iteration-3/index.qmd). The Self-study pages are there when you want to look something up.

### You are a teacher

You are welcome to use the course, or parts of it, in your own teaching: the content is licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and the code under MIT (see the [license](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/blob/main/LICENSE.md)). All notebooks, pages and data are in the [course repository](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml). We'd love to hear how you use it: post in [Show and tell](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/discussions/categories/show-and-tell).

## The course route

Self-study and DataLab take turns: you learn a set of concepts, then apply them in the project, then learn the next set. Follow the steps in this order and take as long as each step needs.

The menu lists all of Self-study before the DataLab, and so does the Next link at the bottom of each page. At the end of each step, a note on the page points you to the next one.

::: {.course-route}
:::

## What you need

- **Prerequisites.** Basic Python, NumPy, pandas and Matplotlib (see the [overview](index.qmd)). If you need a refresher: the [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/), [NumPy for absolute beginners](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html), [10 minutes to pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/10min.html), the [Matplotlib quick start](https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/quick_start.html), or Kaggle's free [Python](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/python) and [pandas](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/pandas) courses. No chemistry is needed: the project explains what you need to know.
- **The textbook.** The reading guides follow Aurélien Géron, *Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras & TensorFlow* (3rd edition, O'Reilly). Many libraries offer it through the O'Reilly learning platform. Without the book you can still do the whole course: the reading guides say what each chapter is about, the [book's own notebooks](https://github.com/ageron/handson-ml3) are free, and the course notebooks stand on their own.
- **A computer** with about 3 GB of free disk space for the [setup](setup.qmd). Any recent Windows, macOS or Linux computer works.

## Working through the notebooks

The notebooks mix explanations with exercises, marked **Your Turn**, and empty cells marked `# YOUR CODE HERE`. Many exercises show the expected output, so you can check your result. Some Self-study notebooks show a worked solution right after an exercise (marked `SOLUTION` or "my solution"), so that you can compare it with your own: try first, then look. All other exercises, and the DataLab project, have no published solutions: working out the code yourself is where the learning happens. Read the documentation of the functions you use, and if you ask an AI assistant, ask it to explain rather than to write the code for you.

## When you are stuck

- **Questions:** ask in the course [Discussions (Q&A)](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/discussions/categories/q-a), and help others when you can. Say which notebook and exercise, what you tried and the full error message. Please share hints and ideas, not complete solutions, so that others can still learn from the exercises.
- **Mistakes in the course:** use **Report an issue** under the table of contents of any page.
- There is no staff support or grading. The course team looks at the Discussions when it can and fixes reported mistakes, but cannot answer every question.

## The Kaggle competitions

Two competitions, stability and energy levels, with a new edition every quarter. The links, how to take part and how they are scored are in [Iteration 3+](datalab/iteration-3/index.qmd#the-kaggle-competitions). You submit for the first time at the end of Iteration 2; expect that first score to be lower than your cross-validation score.
